title: camellia japonica subsp. hortensis
intro: Camellia japonica subsp. hortensis, commonly known as the tea camellia, is a subspecies of Camellia japonica, a plant species native to East Asia and widely cultivated for its flowers and leaves. The tea camellia is valued for its leaves, which can be used to make a tea rich in antioxidants and offer various health benefits, including reducing inflammation and improving cardiovascular health. The leaves of Camellia japonica subsp. hortensis have therapeutic actions, including acting as an antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial agent, which can help protect against cell damage and promote overall well-being. The bioactive constituents of Camellia japonica subsp. hortensis include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and other polyphenolic compounds, which contribute to its medicinal properties and health benefits.
